items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-02
items.q: I went to a couple of times with my wife, Barbara.

ctx.x: And what was the business of Earthquake and Williams? How did that work?

I'm not quite sure how that happened. My understanding was that the, uh, was that Turk and, uh, Pete Kloot, his piano player for a number of years now, and either all or some, or maybe none of the other guys in the band, bought this building sort of on the edge of Chinatown and turned it into a, uh, club called Earthquake Magoons where the Murphy band was entertainment. Uh, it was popular for a number of years. I hear it's been sold now. Oh, this is, this is quite recently. Uh, they added a kind of a mildly…

I really don't know enough about Turk Murphy to ask you. You know, I've heard the rackets, and I've heard him a lot, but not that often. They ask you much more, unless you can think of something else.
